transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-09-23
Start: 15:30 UTC
Duration: ~42m
Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Olivia Chen (SE), Jon Park (SE, partial), Erin Cole (Nova Commerce), Marcus Li (Nova Platform), Nina Alvarez (CPO), Diego Torres (SRE, joined late)

Summary (auto): Quick Console walkthrough focusing on per-route dashboards, usage analytics, and cost breakdown. Discussion of hosted vs dedicated for their footprint, SSO/KMS concerns, and POC next steps. Action items captured at end.

[00:00] Samir: hey everyone thanks for carving out time today's just a quick 30 minute - we booked 45 but we'll try to be crisp - console walkthrough focusing on usage analytics and per route cost breakdown, okay?
[00:18] Erin: yep thanks, excited - Erin here, we run a lot of inference for product search and recommendations, mostly in our k8s cluster today, we want to understand cost and latency tradeoffs.
[00:28] Olivia: cool, I'll share my screen momentarily - show the console. quick question on stack: are you mostly cloud deployed or hybrid?
[00:35] Erin: mostly cloud, GCP, but we have some on-prem for latency-sensitive workloads - some data residency asks too.
[00:42] Samir: got it - good context. action is to show per-route dashboards, token breakdowns, and how we surface cost by route and model variant.

[01:05] [Screen share starts] Olivia: right so landing page first - usage overview: requests, tokens in, tokens out, avg latency, errors. this top chart is a 7-day view, you can change to 24 hours or 30 days. note that token math is auto-derived from the model metadata and your call payloads, but you can upload a prompt set for more accurate estimates.
[01:35] Marcus: are those token numbers pre or post-encoding? we send a lot of unicode docs.
[01:40] Olivia: it's based on the payload we receive, the console shows both raw char count and estimated tokens; occasional miscounting with non-utf8 bytes is possible - we've seen it about ~1-2% difference.

[02:02] Olivia: next section is per-route dashboards - so think of a route as an API path (e.g., /recommendations, /search, /insights). you can filter by model, deployment type (hosted vs dedicated vs private), and time window. route dashboard shows: request volume, p50/p95 latency, tokens per request, cost per 1k requests, and a cost trend.
[02:30] [00:30s speaker overlap] Erin: nice, can you show an example for our search route?
[02:37] Olivia: sure - picking /search - here you see a breakdown by model variant. notice the console calls out compatible fallbacks; if you pin a high-accuracy variant but fall back to a quantized variant during load, we surface the mix and the blended cost.

[03:05] Samir: that's important for us - because on peak traffic we might want graceful degradation to reduce cost but keep latency ok.
[03:12] Erin: how accurate are those blended cost numbers? we need to report to finance.
[03:18] Olivia: cost is computed from per-token model cost plus infra allocation for dedicated pools. for hosted it's straightforward per-token rates. for Dedicated we show an amortized per-token and per-request cost based on committed capacity and observed utilization. there are assumptions, and we provide the model for the math so you can export and validate.

[04:02] [04:00] Marcus: can we export the per-route CSV with breakdown by minute? we need that to run our cost model in-house.
[04:08] Olivia: yes exports allow per-route, per-model, per-minute granularity for 30/90/365 day windows. there is a link: export > csv.

[05:00] Olivia: quick demo of anomaly detection - if cost per route jumps or tokens spike we generate an alert and you can tie to Slack/pager duty etc. you can also pin a budget for a route.
[05:25] Nina: do you show prompt-level tokenization? like are we able to see which prompts are heavy?
[05:30] Olivia: yep, we have top prompt sets and you can tag prompts; you can upload a canonical prompt bank for evals and we map production traffic to those.

[06:10] Samir: question on Dedicated - if you reserve capacity what visibility do you get in the console for utilization?
[06:17] Olivia: dedicated shows pool-level utilization, per-deployment latency heatmaps, and per-route consumption. committed vs actual utilization is shown and we provide suggestions - e.g., reduce pool size or enable burst for x% of the day - suggestions come from Optimize.
[06:40] Erin: do those suggestions include quantization guidance? we noticed some models are expensive but quantizing hurts quality.
[06:47] Olivia: yes Optimize ties model recommendations to historical request profiles; it might suggest 4-bit quant for tail routes and full precision for core routes. you can preview expected cost savings and run canaries.

[07:20] [07:10] Marcus: security - we need audit logs and KMS integration. where do those show up?
[07:26] Samir: good call - KMS/HSM is supported for Private and Dedicated; console shows key usage logs and you can download audit trails. also SOC 2 and ISO docs available - we'll share them.
[07:40] Diego (joined): sorry late - quick question on routing - can you route by latency SLO or cost?
[07:46] Olivia: yes policy engine supports latency-first, cost-first, region-first. you can create policies per route; e.g., /search latency-first, fallback to cheaper variant after 150ms.

[08:25] [08:20] Erin: can we simulate a cost forecast for a seasonal spike? we have Black Friday style traffic.
[08:30] Olivia: in the console forecast tool you can input expected qps and percent long context requests - it will simulate cost and show whether Dedicated commit would be cheaper vs hosted. we also show break-even line and recommended commit size.

[09:05] Samir: real world note: customers with heavy bursty traffic often use a small Dedicated pool for steady baseline and hosted for burst - gives best of both.

[09:40] [09:35] Marcus: any limitations on per-route retention for usage logs? we have compliance needs.
[09:45] Olivia: retention tiers available - standard 90 days, enterprise 365, custom on request with additional cost. audit logs retention can be extended.

[10:10] Erin: about billing - how granular will invoices be? finance needs per-product chargeback.
[10:16] Samir: invoices can be per-route or per-team depending on how you tag routes; the console supports cost allocation tags and exports for chargebacks.

[11:05] [11:00] Olivia: quick walkthrough of the cost breakdown UI: top shows total cost for selected window, then model-level cost pie chart, then route-level table with columns: route name, requests, tokens, avg latency, model variant, estimated cost, and cost per 1k requests. you can sort and drill into a route to see per-minute heatmap and example request samples (sampled for privacy).

[12:00] [12:00] Erin: do you surface per-token pricing for open models vs our private model? we might run a private transformer in our VPC.
[12:08] Olivia: for private models (on-prem/VPC) the console shows an infra amortization line plus any licensing. per-token rate is adjustable - we surface it so you can compare apples to apples.

[12:45] Samir: competitor question often comes up - how is this different from running your own infra? we typically highlight the runtime optimizations, continuous batching, and smart routing + the billing/ops layer.

[12:58] Erin: yeah, our infra team worries about ops burden.

[13:20] Olivia: also we do built-in KV cache and prefix caching which reduces token spend on sessioned chat; console shows cache hit rates per route.

[14:05] [14:00] Marcus: gonna ask the nitty gritty - how do you surface quantization impact on quality? we need to show product owners.
[14:13] Olivia: Optimize runs regression checks against saved eval prompts, and you can run A/B canaries where we route X% to quantized and X% to full precision and gather metric diffs. console surfaces perplexity-like proxies and custom metrics you provide.

[15:00] Erin: any limits on the sample size for those canaries? we have low volume for some niche routes.
[15:06] Olivia: you can do longer windows; smallest is 0.1% traffic but you can also run offline evals with your prompt set.

[16:00] [16:00] Diego: network question - if we do Private deployment behind our VPC, will console still have the same analytics?
[16:08] Samir: we'll deploy a lightweight agent that emits metrics to your Private control plane and then we aggregate - yes console parity is maintained but with different retention and export controls.

[17:00] [17:00] Olivia: quick demo of export and report generation - show how to download a per-route cost breakdown and attach to the invoice.

[18:05] Erin: any obvious gotchas you see for migration from our current k8s endpoints to Redwood?
[18:12] Samir: biggest is traffic shaping and token accounting - we recommend a short POC ingesting a day or two of traffic into our benchmark harness to estimate realistic costs. Also, if you use strict internal auth, we'll need SAML/SSO mapping work.

[19:00] Olivia: here's an example export - open CSV shows columns with estimated_token_in, token_out, model_variant, infra_alloc, and amortized_cost. note sometimes proper nouns like model names get mangled in the ASR, but the export itself is clean.

[20:08] Nina: product question - can business users see these dashboards w/o access to secrets? we need RBAC.
[20:15] Olivia: RBAC is supported; we have viewer, analyst, admin roles; viewers see dashboards and exports but not keys or model rollout controls.

[21:00] [21:00] Samir: ok let's cover next steps and POC. thinking: 2-week pilot, ingest 3 days of traffic slice, run latency + cost bench, evaluate Dedicated commit recommendation.
[21:20] Erin: sounds reasonable. timeline wise we'd like results before Oct 6.

[22:05] Olivia: I'll prepare a benchmark template and a POC plan. Samir will follow up with pricing and Dedicated scenarios.

[22:25] Marcus: just flagging compliance - we'll need SOC2 docs and KMS integration details before legal signs.

[23:00] [23:00] Brief period of cross talk about exact routes to include.

[24:10] Erin: one more - what about aggregated cost per product line? can we tag by team?
[24:18] Olivia: yes route tags and team tags allow aggregation and chargeback; console supports multi-dim grouping.

[25:00] [25:00] Diego: small note: we need certs for egress IP allowlisting - how does that work for hosted?
[25:07] Samir: hosted supports static egress ranges for allowlisting for enterprise customers; Dedicated gives you fixed IPs too. we'll include IP ranges.

[26:20] Olivia: demo wrap: the customer can run a what-if simulation, export supporting CSVs, and set alerts. the UI also has a drilldown to example requests and top prompt sets.

[27:10] Erin: ok let's capture action items.

[27:30] Samir: action items recap - Samir send pricing and Dedicated proposal; Olivia send benchmark template and run initial test; Erin share traffic profile and SLOs; Marcus share KMS/network constraints.

[28:00] Nina: also please include any potential cost savings numbers for a split dedicated+hosted approach.

[28:20] Samir: we'll include a break-even analysis and a recommended commit.

[29:00] [30:00] quick micro-conversation about dates, availability.

[31:00] Diego: if we go forward how long to onboard before we see metrics in console?
[31:06] Olivia: basic metrics appear within minutes of traffic hitting Redwood gateway; full attribution and cost calibration usually within 24 hours after sample ingestion.

[32:00] Erin: ok that works. last vendor question - do you have an SLA for latency on dedicated?
[32:07] Samir: yes dedicated includes SLA-backed p95 latency targets, we can share the SLA doc.

[33:00] [33:00] short closing notes.

[34:00] [END]

Notes about transcription: there are some ASR artifacts (e.g., "KV cash" instead of "KV cache", "Redwood Dediate" for "Dedicated") and occasional speaker mislabels. Full exports and CSVs referenced in the call will be attached to the meeting in CRM.
